raw_payload.title: The Voice on the Line
raw_payload.summary: A transcriber listening through one microphone also hears everyone near it. We train causal voice isolators that keep only the caller for a speech recogniser: masking transformers with 20 ms of latency that enroll the caller from the call itself. Short evaluation windows hide two failures that real calls expose: forgetting the caller when another voice talks alone for a while, and damaging a caller who is alone. Long calls with turns, memory beyond the attention window and real headset crosstalk address the first, at a cost to the second. WavLM-Large's own weights, made causal and trained inside the model, move that trade, and training windows cut from longer calls remove most of a lone caller's cold start. The release (555M parameters) makes 16.13% word errors on 60 s AMI windows, against 23.66% for VoxLock, the strongest open isolator, and 14.77% on average over nine test sets, against 18.04%; it is level on Krisp's benchmark, and a caller who is alone still loses more words than with VoxLock. Distilled without WavLM into 22.1M and 9.8M parameters, it runs live on one CPU thread inside a LiveKit agent, at 12.5% and 8.5% of a core per call, with 10.66% and 10.99% error on our development sets (the release 10.49%). In an agent that talks back, noise interrupts it 0.54 times a minute of its speech behind our agent model, which gates its output on a caller-presence head, against 1.18 for VoxLock. We open-source the models, with a LiveKit plugin, at https://huggingface.co/collections/Scicom-intl/voice-isolator.
